In brief: The upcoming week is expected to be characterized by a persistent low-pressure system that will bring elevated rain chances to Abuja, with temperatures remaining relatively consistent and humidity levels remaining high throughout the period. ### Monday A low-pressure system will dominate the weather pattern over Abuja, leading to a high chance of rainfall throughout the day. The temperature will rise to a high of 28°C, while the low will be 21°C, resulting in a moderate diurnal temperature range. The humidity will be exceptionally high, at 94%, making the heat index feel more like 30°C. In areas such as Maitama and Garki, the urban heat island effect will be pronounced, making the temperature feel even warmer. The wind will be light and variable, blowing at a speed of 2 km/h, which will do little to alleviate the sweltering conditions. As the day progresses, the rain will become more widespread, with the heaviest downpours expected in the late afternoon and early evening. The models suggest that the rainfall accumulation will be in the range of 20-30 mm, which may lead to flooding in low-lying areas such as the sections of the airport road that are prone to waterlogging.
The rain will be most intense in the late afternoon, around the time when many residents are commuting home from work. The roads may become congested, especially in areas such as Wuse and Gwarinpa, where the traffic is already heavy during rush hour. The good news is that the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway traffic is currently light, which may help to mitigate the impact of the rain on the commute. However, the rain may still cause significant disruptions, especially for those who have to navigate the roads in the affected areas. The low-pressure system will continue to dominate the weather pattern throughout the day, with the rain showers becoming more scattered in the evening. The temperature will dip to a low of 21°C, resulting in a relatively pleasant evening, despite the high humidity. In areas such as Aso Rock and the surroundings of the National Assembly, the cooler evening temperatures will provide some relief from the heat of the day. The models indicate that the low-pressure system will persist over Abuja for the next few days, leading to a prolonged period of elevated rain chances. While it is difficult to predict the exact timing and intensity of the rainfall, my best guess is that the rain will continue to be a significant feature of the weather pattern throughout the week.
